jobs.description:
**JOB ANNOUNCEMENT**

The Community Youth Center of San Francisco (CYC) provides the youth of our city a sense of belonging and vital tools and experiences to succeed in life. Our services include academic support and college counseling, job placement and employment training, substance use and violence prevention education, crisis intervention and mediation, leadership development, technology and computer training. Our mission is to encourage a diverse population of high-need young people to explore their full potential through academic, career, family, and community life.  
  
**Title:****Program Coordinator - YAWL Young Adult Job Centers**

**Salary:****$30.00 - $34.00 per hour plus excellent benefits**

**Reports to:****Program Supervisor**

**Status:****Full-Time, (40 hours/week), Non-Exempt**  
  
**Program Summary:** CYC’s YAWL Workforce Development Program provides job readiness and employment support services to youth ages 16-24. The program offers 1:1 job search and career coaching, work based learning internships, college and career exploration, and job shadowing opportunities to propel youth and young adults to be ready for college, work and reach productive adulthood.  
  
**Position Description:** Under the supervision of the Program Supervisor, the Program Coordinator is responsible for overseeing the Young Adult Job Center portfolio, supervising staff, overseeing workshops/trainings, establishing best practice program models, and providing high quality youth workforce and development services.  
  
**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Oversee the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Young Adult Work Link program and comprehensive service delivery model.
* Develop policy and procedure recommendations to strengthen the program model and collaboration among grantee and coalition partners.
* Ensure program development and service delivery align with “Youth Program Quality Standards” and meet all “Work Plan” deliverables and deadlines.
* Complete all required documentation, reports, and program deliverables in a timely manner.
* Lead citywide outreach and recruitment efforts, cultivating strategic community partnerships and developing a robust referral network to support recruitment and engagement, with a focus on priority populations.
* Conduct participant assessments and provide intensive case management, wraparound supportive services, and guidance to address barriers affecting work and school performance.
* Develop individualized vocational goals and career plans using vocational and interest assessments, and provide personal and career guidance.
* Develop and facilitate job readiness training workshops, including but not limited to professionalism, career exploration, resume and cover letter building, job search/navigation, interview skill development, mock interviews, and strength/talent identification.
* Coordinate GED attainment, tutoring, basic skills remediation, postsecondary education, and workforce training services.
* Provide 1:1 career guidance and assist participants with individualized education and career planning services, job search and placement assistance and conduct follow ups for retention services.
* Connect participants to resources within CYC and other CBO or city services for barrier removal to ensure their success.
* Supervise, support, coach and train Program Specialists in job readiness training content, career counseling, outreach, funder databases, and other duties as applicable.
* Collaborate with the workforce team to strategize on program planning, development and implementation of overall youth workforce development programs and outcomes.
* Coordinate career exploration events and adult mentoring opportunities such as worksite/company tours, college tours, and networking events for program participants
* Cultivate relationships with employers, developing jobs for youth and young adults.
* Support agency-wide events and perform other duties as assigned by management.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's degree in relevant field.
* Experience working with diverse youth backgrounds, preferably within youth workforce development programs.
* Previous experience in program coordination and development.
* Ability to work with ethnically diverse groups of low-income youth as well as English learners to support their social and emotional needs during transition.
* At least 1 year of experience supervising a team of three or more staff.
* Experience working with San Francisco's diverse communities and neighborhoods.
* Experience working with community-based service providers and private sector partners.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills and proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Zoom, and other technology platforms.
* Experience facilitating workshops for youth and young adults.
* Ability to work as part of a team, to prioritize and handle multiple tasks and to work independently in a high-pressure environment.
* Bilingual in Cantonese/Mandarin/Spanish and English is preferred.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills.
* Ability to work some evenings and weekends.
* Enthusiasm for promoting academic achievement and college education.
* Able to lift or move at least 25lbs

CYC is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and will not discriminate against any applicant or employee on the basis of race, age, religion, gender, marital status, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other basis recognized by federal, state, or local law, including on the basis of the intersection of two or more protected characteristics, also known as intersectional discrimination. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment.

A career at Optima MMG is an opportunity to be part of a dynamic and forward-thinking organization. We encourage continuous learning and professional growth, providing our employees with access to industry experts, cutting-edge technologies, and a supportive community that values each individual's contributions. Join us on this journey to not only advance your career but to be a driving force in transforming lives and communities through passionate and fulfilling work!

**Job Summary:**

The Community Health Worker (CHW) serves as a trusted liaison between community members, healthcare providers, and social service organizations. Working as an integral, mostly remote member of the pod's interdisciplinary Care Team, alongside Lead Care Managers, MAs, and RNs, the CHW is responsible for conducting outreach, providing health education, addressing social determinants of health, and connecting members to medical, behavioral health, and community-based resources. Under the general supervision of Enhanced Care Management Leadership, the CHW works closely with members, families, care teams, and community partners to improve health outcomes, promote self-sufficiency, and reduce barriers to care; working mainly remotely alongside the Lead Care Managers for direct member engagement. This position requires strong communication skills, cultural sensitivity, and a passion for serving diverse populations.

  

**Responsibilities:**

* Serve as the primary team member to conduct in-person visits to community members and provide education on health-related topics.

* Assist individuals in accessing healthcare services, social services, and community resources.

* Assess social determinants of health and identify barriers impacting member well-being and healthcare access.

* Support care coordination activities and collaborate with healthcare providers, care managers, social workers, and community agencies.

* Function as an integral, mostly remote member of the pod Care Team, partnering closely with Lead Care Managers, MAs, and RNs who conduct direct member engagement.

* Accompany members to appointments when appropriate and assist with healthcare system, insurance program, and benefit enrollment navigation.

* Maintain ongoing contact with members through phone calls, home visits, community outreach, and telehealth platforms.

* Document member interactions, assessments, and referrals accurately and timely in designated systems.

* Advocate for members and assist with resolving barriers that interfere with access to care and services.

* Participate in community outreach events, health fairs, educational workshops, and engagement activities.

* Maintain member confidentiality and comply with all organizational and regulatory requirements.

* Participate in regularly scheduled member huddles for updates and feedback.

* Reporting in-person to the office as needed for meetings.

* Perform additional duties as assigned.

  

**Populations of Focus:**

* **Individuals experiencing homelessness:** Lacking a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence.

* **Individuals at risk for avoidable hospital or emergency department utilization:** Five or more emergency room visits in a six-month period that could have been avoided with appropriate outpatient care or improved treatment adherence.

* **Individuals with Serious Mental Health and/ or substance use disorder needs:** Adults who meet the eligibility criteria for participation in, or obtaining services through Specialist mental health services or the Drug Medi-Cal organized delivery system or Drug Medi-Cal program.

* **Individuals transitioning from incarceration/Justice Involved:** Adults transitioning from a correctional setting or transitioned from a correction setting within the past 12 months, or children and youth who are transitioning from a youth correctional facility or transitioned from being in a youth correctional facility within the past 12 months.

* **Adults living in the community and at risk for long-term care institutionalization:** Adults who are living in the community who meet the SNF Level of Care criteria; or who require lower-acuity skilled nursing or equipment for prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of acute illness or injury.

* **Adult nursing facility residents transitioning to the community:** Adult nursing residents who are interested in moving out of the institution, and are likely candidates to do so successfully, and are able to reside continuously in the community.

* **Children and youth enrolled in California Children's Services (CCS) or CCS Whole Child Model (WCM) with Additional Needs Beyond the CCS condition:** Children and youth enrolled in CCS or CCS WCM and are experiencing at least one complex social factor influencing their health.

Meta is seeking an experienced U.S. Immigration Program Manager to drive the operating model and program direction for U.S. employment-based immigration, serving as a subject-matter expert on case filings and compliance operations. This role is accountable for filing quality, accuracy, and timeliness at scale, the program's U.S. compliance posture, and the frameworks, playbooks, and tooling that underpin delivery.This individual will partner closely with Recruiting, People Partners, Legal, external counsel, and business leaders to solve the most complex U.S. immigration challenges, ensure regulatory compliance, and continuously improve our case management operations. This is a senior individual contributor role operating with significant autonomy: identifying program priorities, resolving ambiguous cross-functional problems, and influencing decisions without direct authority.  
  
  

### **US Immigration Program Manager (Strategy & Operations) Responsibilities:**

* Own the design, maintenance, and continuous improvement of Meta's U.S. immigration operating model and compliance framework, including decision rights and controls for right-to-work verification, government reporting, audit readiness, and regulatory change management, in partnership with Legal, HR, and outside counsel
* Serve as a senior subject-matter expert on U.S. employment-based nonimmigrant and immigrant filings (e.g., H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN, PERM, EB-1/NIW/EB-2/EB-3, adjustment of status, and consular processing), partnering with Legal and outside counsel on case strategy, filing requirements, and adjudication trends
* Own program-level oversight of complex, high-profile, and time-sensitive immigration filings, personally leading selected escalations while scaling case preparation and execution through operational teams and outside counsel
* Develop and maintain standardized filing playbooks, templates, checklists, and quality-control protocols that enable consistent, high-quality case preparation at scale
* Monitor U.S. regulatory developments and proactively translate new requirements into updated policies, processes, and operational guidance with Legal and outside counsel
* coordinate with regional immigration leads where cases have cross-border dependencies
* Drive technology and process innovation in case management workflows: identifying opportunities for automation, AI-assisted checks with human review, and system enhancements to reduce cycle times and improve accuracy
* Act as an escalation point for complex filing scenarios, RFEs (Requests for Evidence), denials, and novel immigration questions, partnering with Legal and outside counsel on resolution paths and addressing systemic causes through process improvements
* Establish and enforce quality standards and SLAs for external immigration counsel and service providers, reviewing work product and driving accountability for filing accuracy and timeliness
* Partner cross-functionally with Legal, People Partners, Recruiting, and Finance to align U.S. immigration operations with workforce planning and talent strategy, resolve competing priorities, and clarify handoffs, with the PERM recruitment team owning recruitment execution and this role owning overall immigration case progression
* Develop compliance dashboards, reporting mechanisms, and audit processes that provide visibility into filing volumes, cycle times, compliance health, and risk exposure, and use these measures to prioritize improvements and hold teams and vendors accountable
* Set and drive a multi-quarter roadmap for the U.S. immigration program, identifying high-impact problems, making the case for investment, and sequencing initiatives against business priorities, risk, and delivery capacity with minimal management oversight

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 12+ years of progressive experience in U.S. employment-based immigration with responsibility for case filings, compliance program design, and immigration operations, including end-to-end ownership of complex programs at scale
* Deep subject-matter expertise across U.S. employment-based nonimmigrant visa categories and permanent residence pathways, including PERM, immigrant petitions, adjustment of status, and consular processing
* Demonstrated experience designing and operating U.S. immigration compliance frameworks, setting program direction, and establishing decision rights and controls across teams and external providers
* Track record of developing scalable processes, playbooks, and quality frameworks that deliver measurable improvements across multiple teams
* Experience managing relationships with external law firms and immigration vendors, including setting quality expectations and enforcing SLAs
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders (Legal, HR, Recruiting, Finance), resolve competing priorities, and drive decisions in ambiguous situations without direct authority
* Experience leveraging AI or automation tools to drive efficiency in compliance monitoring and case processing workflows

* Experience operating within a global technology company or a similarly complex, high-volume immigration environment
* Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
* Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)

jobs.description:
Legal and Compliance Operations is seeking an Automation Program Manager to help us automate high-volume review at scale across Legal and Compliance workflows. Our workflows run on a composite of LLM-based decisioning, rules-based logic that encodes policy directly, and signals drawn from reporter history, content matching and behavioral patterns. Automation now carries a substantial share of enforcement volume, which means its quality determines both the legal risk we mitigate and the experience of the rights holders, regulators and people who depend on these decisions.As an Automation Program Manager, you will own the measured quality of assigned automations. Half of the role is forward motion: taking an automation from where it performs today to where the operational plan requires, through iteration on prompts, rules and signal thresholds. The other half is regression response: when reliability, correctness, precision or recall degrades, you find out why and drive it back. An effective candidate in this role is rigorous about measurement, comfortable working across all three automation types, and able to tell a genuine regression apart from a shift in what is arriving.  
  
  

### **Automation Program Manager, Legal and Compliance Operations Responsibilities:**

* Hill-climb reliability (prompt, iterate and improve), correctness, precision and recall on assigned automations across Legal and Compliance Workflows
* Iterate on LLM components, including prompts, task decomposition, routing, and abstention and fallback behavior
* Diagnose and improve rules-based components, including coverage, ordering and precedence, conflicts between rules, rules firing on the wrong population, and rules that stop matching after a policy or schema change
* Tune signal-based components, including thresholds, signal freshness and availability, and the precision cost of upstream signal drift
* Investigate regressions to isolate whether the cause is model, rule, signal, upstream data, policy change, or a shift in the incoming population, and distinguish real degradation from volume mix shift
* Drive regressions to a measured recovery that holds across a following measurement period, and document what degraded, why it was not caught earlier, and what detection would have caught it
* Build and maintain offline eval and gold standard data sets, coordinating expert-review sampling with the reviewers who hold the ground truth
* Build regression detection that surfaces degradation before the next reporting cycle, and close measurement coverage gaps so automations that are live are also measured
* Build scripts, notebooks and internal tooling so program managers and operations leads can run measurement independently
* Document what was tried, what moved the metric, and what did not, so subsequent workflows start further along

* Working knowledge of Python and SQL, with experience pulling a dataset, computing precision and recall, and segmenting results to locate where loss is concentrated

**Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!**

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. ### **Job Description**

We have an opening for a **Research & Development (R&D) Radiation Generating Device (RGD) & Sealed Radioactive Source (SRS) Program Lead** within the Radiation Protection Functional Area. This position independently plans and executes Research and Development (R&D) efforts supporting the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of LLNL’s Radiation Generating Devices and Sealed Radioactive Source Safety programs. The RGD/SRS Program Lead works independently, with minimal direction, to plan and execute research and development (R&D) efforts within the context of applying science technological and R&D engineering to anticipate, innovate, and deliver program solutions to the Laboratory’s mission. This position is in the Environment, Safety and Health (ESH) Directorate, within the Radiological Protection Functional Area (RPFA).

*This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization.*

This position is subject to DOE Order 426.2, *Personnel Selection, Training, Qualification, and Certification Requirements for DOE Nuclear Facilities*. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level.

**You will**

* Set specific technical strategy and direction for the Radiation Generating Device and Sealed Radioactive Source Safety Programs, serving as the technical expert RGD, accelerators, and high activity sealed sources across LLNL and the Department of Energy (DOE) complex.
* Assist in the development of shielding and design verification in order to solve complex radiological source problems introduced by RGDs and high activity sealed radioactive sources requiring in-depth analysis of tangible and intangible factors, including regulatory requirements, program needs, and variable work environments.
* Provide radiological oversight during annual compliance surveys for High-Risk RGDs, verifying that administrative and engineering controls remain effective and identifying corrective actions where deficiencies are found.
* Develop radiological survey plans addressing non-uniform radiation fields produced by pulsed devices, accounting for the unique measurement and instrumentation considerations these fields present.
* Work independently, with minimal direction, using independent judgment to determine methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for RGD/SRS Safety Program design meeting requirements and expectations of DOE O 420.2E, 10 CFR 835, and DOE G 441.1C.

new_jobs.description:
Legal and Compliance Operations is seeking an Automation Program Manager to help us automate high-volume review at scale across Legal and Compliance workflows. Our workflows run on a composite of LLM-based decisioning, rules-based logic that encodes policy directly, and signals drawn from reporter history, content matching and behavioral patterns. Automation now carries a substantial share of enforcement volume, which means its quality determines both the legal risk we mitigate and the experience of the rights holders, regulators and people who depend on these decisions.As an Automation Program Manager, you will own the measured quality of assigned automations. Half of the role is forward motion: taking an automation from where it performs today to where the operational plan requires, through iteration on prompts, rules and signal thresholds. The other half is regression response: when reliability, correctness, precision or recall degrades, you find out why and drive it back. An effective candidate in this role is rigorous about measurement, comfortable working across all three automation types, and able to tell a genuine regression apart from a shift in what is arriving.  
  
  

### **Automation Program Manager, Legal and Compliance Operations Responsibilities:**

* Hill-climb reliability (prompt, iterate and improve), correctness, precision and recall on assigned automations across Legal and Compliance Workflows
* Iterate on LLM components, including prompts, task decomposition, routing, and abstention and fallback behavior
* Diagnose and improve rules-based components, including coverage, ordering and precedence, conflicts between rules, rules firing on the wrong population, and rules that stop matching after a policy or schema change
* Tune signal-based components, including thresholds, signal freshness and availability, and the precision cost of upstream signal drift
* Investigate regressions to isolate whether the cause is model, rule, signal, upstream data, policy change, or a shift in the incoming population, and distinguish real degradation from volume mix shift
* Drive regressions to a measured recovery that holds across a following measurement period, and document what degraded, why it was not caught earlier, and what detection would have caught it
* Build and maintain offline eval and gold standard data sets, coordinating expert-review sampling with the reviewers who hold the ground truth
* Build regression detection that surfaces degradation before the next reporting cycle, and close measurement coverage gaps so automations that are live are also measured
* Build scripts, notebooks and internal tooling so program managers and operations leads can run measurement independently
* Document what was tried, what moved the metric, and what did not, so subsequent workflows start further along

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 2+ years of relevant experience in data annotation, labeling, quality assurance, or content review operations, including time spent close to automated decision output
* Experience with guideline accuracy and inter-rater agreement, including diagnosing why qualified reviewers disagree
* Working knowledge of Python and SQL, with experience pulling a dataset, computing precision and recall, and segmenting results to locate where loss is concentrated
* Experience reading and reasoning about conditional logic to trace how a decision was reached
* Experience working with large operational datasets in a notebook environment
* Investigative approach to metric movement, identifying cause rather than the explanation that fits
* Experience communicating results clearly, including reporting a metric that has not moved or a regression that is not yet explained

* Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
